newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's union groups vow to reopen strikes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's union groups vow to reopen strikes.

text.p: South Korea's two union unbrella groups said on Thursday they would re-start strikes soon after the New Year holidays to back their demand for the withdrawal of a controversial labour law.

"About 50 unions comprising around 100,000 members in the auto and other manufacturing industries will go on strike again from Friday moring," said Kang Hoon-jung, a spokesman for the outlawed Korea Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU).
"The rest of our 500,000 members from hospitals, Hyundai companies and other manufacturers will join the work stoppage from Monday as their New Year holidays end on Sunday."
On January 7, subway and broadcast unions are set to strike, the KCTU said.

Nationwide strikes erupted on December 26, paralysing most major industries, after the ruling New Korea Party rammed a labour law through parliament that gives employers the right to lay off workers, hire temporary staff and replace strikers.
Strikes were called off for the New Year holidays.

The confederation said it represented unions at automakers, including Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest carmaker, Kia Motors Corp, and shipyards, including Hyundai Heavy Industries Co and Daewoo Heavy Industries Co.
"Strikes will continue until our demands are met," Kang said.
The nation's largest umbrella union group, the Federation of Korean Trade Unions (FKTU), said it would launch strikes again "if the government and employers try to resolve the issue with force".
"We plan to organise a large-scale rally on January 10 and call for a general strike by all members from January 11," said federation spokesman Min Dong-won.
The FKTU said its second round of strikes would be led by unions in the public and service sectors.
The two umbrella union groups claim an aggregate 1.7 million members in most of South Korea's major industries and public-sector services.
